entrada-deus-01.context: The Bible does not begin by trying to prove that God exists: it begins with him already acting. Its first hearers knew stories of many gods at war. Here, before anything else, there is one God, and he creates.
entrada-deus-01.focusQuestion: What changes in you when you know God was already there before everything, even before your own story?
entrada-deus-01.keywordGloss: The start of everything that exists; when it comes, God is already there.
facts: God created the heavens and the earth.
In the beginning, the earth was formless and empty.
The Spirit of God hovered over the waters.
God spoke, and the light came to be.
God saw that the light was good.
God called the light Day and the darkness Night.

entrada-deus-02.context: Moses had fled Egypt and lived in the desert tending sheep. From the bush that burned without burning up, God calls him to bring Israel out of slavery. Moses hesitates and asks what to say when the people want to know who sent him.
entrada-deus-02.focusQuestion: Moses asked "who am I?" and God answered by saying who he is. Where do you need to look more at God than at yourself?
entrada-deus-02.keywordGloss: The name God reveals to Moses: he is who he is, depends on no one, and is with his people.
facts: Moses asks who he is to go to Pharaoh.
God promises to be with Moses.
Moses asks what name he will tell the people.
God answers: I AM WHO I AM.
God presents himself as the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
God says this is his name forever.

entrada-deus-03.context: Uzziah reigned over Judah for many years, and his death left the people insecure. That same year, the prophet Isaiah is in the temple and receives a vision: he sees who is truly on the throne.
entrada-deus-03.focusQuestion: How does God's holiness change the way you come near to him?
entrada-deus-03.keywordGloss: Set apart, pure, and unlike anything that exists; said three times, it marks what God is to the highest degree.
facts: Isaiah saw the Lord seated on a high and lofty throne.
Each seraph had six wings.
The seraphim proclaimed that the Lord is holy, holy, holy.
The whole earth is full of God's glory.
The house was filled with smoke.
Isaiah admits he is a man of unclean lips.

entrada-deus-04.context: David tended sheep before he became king. He knew what a shepherd does: leads to pasture and water, guides along the way, and defends from danger. In this psalm, he uses that image to speak of the Lord himself.
entrada-deus-04.focusQuestion: In what part of your path do you need to remember that the Lord is with you?
entrada-deus-04.keywordGloss: One who guides, feeds, and protects the sheep; David gives this name to the Lord.
facts: David calls the Lord his shepherd.
The Lord leads David beside the still waters.
In the valley of the shadow of death, David fears no evil.
The Lord's rod and staff bring comfort.
The Lord prepares a feast in front of David's enemies.
Goodness and mercy follow David every day.

entrada-deus-05.context: John opens his Gospel with the same words as Genesis: "No princípio". He calls Jesus the Word, that is, the Word of God. Before telling what Jesus did, John says who he is and where he comes from.
entrada-deus-05.focusQuestion: Looking at Jesus, what do you learn about what God is like?
entrada-deus-05.keywordGloss: The Word of God; John uses this name for Jesus, who shows God in person.
facts: The Word was with God and was God.
All things were made through the Word.
The light shines in the darkness, and the darkness has not overcome it.
John the Baptist came to bear witness to the light, but he was not the light.
Whoever receives the Word gains the right to become a child of God.
The Word became flesh and lived among us.
